title: Jake Reiner Gives Emotional First Interview After Devastating Loss Of Parents Rob And Michele Reiner
text:
Photo by Paul Archuleta/Getty Images

Jake Reiner gave his first television interview since his parents Michele and Rob Reiner were brutally murdered.

In an interview with KABC-TV’s Mark Cota-Robles released August 27, Jake opened up about the harsh reality of losing more than half his family at the same time.

“It’s been 8 months. It feels like 8 years at the same time, and it also feels like 8 minutes,” he said. “Because every moment that I wake up, I’m reminded of my reality.”

Jake spoke fondly of his late parents, who were allegedly stabbed to death by his brother, Nick.

“My parents had unconditional love for all three of us,” he said.

He also recalled the fateful phone call from his sister, Romy, on Dec. 14, 2025, that forever changed the course of his life.

“Romy told me our dad was dead and then she said, ‘I can’t find mom,’” Jake said.

Both his parents were found dead inside their home, and within hours, his brother Nick was arrested.

NEW YORK, NY - APRIL 28: Honoree Rob Reiner poses with family at the 41st Annual Chaplin Award Gala at Avery Fisher Hall at Lincoln Center for the Performing Arts on April 28, 2014 in New York City. (Photo by Michael Loccisano/Getty Images)

Jake expressed the profound grief of losing his parents while his brother remained behind bars, leaving him and Romy to pick up the shattered pieces of their lives.

“Yeah. I mean, he’s in jail, so… ,” he said, seemingly out of words to describe the weight of his feelings.

“You know, it’s… I physically lost my parents. And then Nick was arrested. And now it’s me and Romy,” Jake said. (RELATED: REPORT: Nick Reiner Demands Trust Fund Left By Parents Michele, Rob Reiner, While Awaiting Murder Trial)

Los Angeles Premiere Of MPX Releasing’s “Things Like This”

LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA - MAY 13: Romy Reiner (L) and Jake Reiner (R) attend the Los Angeles premiere of “Things Like This” at Landmark Theatres Sunset on May 13, 2025 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Paul Archuleta/Getty Images)

KABC-TV reported that Jake was restricted from revealing certain information due to the ongoing trial, and noted that although he was comfortable speaking publicly for the first time, Romy was not yet ready to do the same.

Nick remains behind bars after being indicted on two counts of first-degree murder in the deaths of his parents. He has pleaded not guilty, and was denied access to the trust fund his parents left for him, which he intended to use to defend himself in court.
